description:
Prove that core commands succeed, and claim commands fail with the typed git-requirement error, when no git executable is available.

## Background

- Existing tests cover a directory outside any repository with git present: the core lifecycle (`crates/jit/tests/cli_repo_workflow/profile_no_git_lifecycle_tests.rs:46`) and claims failing with exit 10 (`crates/jit/tests/cli_repo_workflow/claim_integration_tests.rs:1189` onwards).
- No test runs commands with no git executable. `crates/jit/tests/cli_issue/search_exit_status_tests.rs:42` runs `search` with an empty `PATH`, which shows only that startup survives.
- Without an executable the layout probe cannot start, so the checkout is classified as outside git, and claims report `REQUIRES_GIT` with exit 10 (`@/charter/D-4`).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A `cli_repo_workflow` module runs `init`, `issue create`, `issue show`, `query available` and `dep add` inside a git repository with a `PATH` holding no git executable, and asserts that each succeeds.
- [hard] REQ-02: The module runs each claim subcommand (`acquire`, `release`, `renew`, `heartbeat`, `status`, `list`, `force-evict`) with no git executable and asserts `REQUIRES_GIT` with exit 10. Against the claim code before the typed mapping, `claim list` exits 3 with `REPOSITORY_NOT_FOUND`, so the test fails there.

## Notes

- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.
title: CLI tests for commands with no git executable
